Pass & Play vs solo Quiet Arcade — how to choose

Compare solo and current NoCharge Pass & Play sessions: one person or two sharing a device, with no online mode or saved game records.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Check the current platform.

Use the public pages behind this explanation.

Open the ArcadeReview PrivacyKeyboard-only play notes

Bottom line: Solo Arcade games are played by one person; Pass & Play is for two people taking turns on one device. Both run in the browser without online matchmaking or a player account, and neither mode saves game records in NoCharge V2.

Side by side

QuestionSolo gamePass & Play
PlayersOne personTwo people sharing one device
Turn flowOne player controls the sessionThe current game names the next player or artist
Network or accountNot requiredNot required; no online matchmaking
Saved recordNo game score or progress record in current V2No match history or result record in current V2

Current Pass & Play titles

The current same-device set includes Checkers, Dots & Boxes, Gomoku, Nine Men’s Morris, Pass the Picture, and Reversi. These are open-information boards or a shared drawing. Each page handles turn changes in its own way; there is no universal handoff screen.

Choose by company and rules

Pick a solo puzzle when you want to think through one board on your own. Pick Pass & Play when another person is beside you and you want a local turn-taking game. The exact controls, board, and objective vary by title, so check the current game page before starting.

What neither mode provides

There is no online opponent, cross-device sync, rating system, player-name history, or saved match dashboard. The active board is held in the page session and resets when a new game is started or the page is reloaded. For current browser storage and processing details, read the Privacy page.
